newsitem.title: USA: Reich sees no sign of wage-push inflation - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Reich sees no sign of wage-push inflation - RFTV.

text.p: Labor Secretary Robert Reich Friday said he saw no sign of wage-push inflation at this point in the economic expansion.

Interviewed on Reuters Financial Televsion following release of the unemployment report that showed continued increases in hourly earnings, Reich said "we dont have yet have any data that those wages are pushing up inflation."
He said employers are being able to offset these increases with substantially lower health care costs.
Asked whether the unemployment rate, which rose to 5.2 percent in September from 5.1 percent in the prior month, could still go lower, he said that was certainly possible.
"I think it's still possible to go further," he said, noting that the rate in some parts of the United States was already lower than that.

He also said there was growing evidence that the economy had slowed to a more sustainable pace, estimating that the third quarter could grow in the 3.0 percent range, or possibly lower, down from Q2's 4.8 percent rate.
White House Council of Economic Advisers Chairman Joseph Stiglitz later said the jobs report was "consistent with our view that the economy is continuing on its path of steady, sustained expansion."

"All recent indicators suggest that the economy will continue on a healthy and balanced course of low unemployment, low inflation and solid economic growth, with all Americans increasingly sharing in the benefits...," he said in a statement.
